Promote frequently-repeated triplets to validation trials

assign_validation_from_frequency.Rd

Companion to find_frequent_triplets: given a candidate set of triplets (its output, or a threshold-filtered subset of it), sets sampleAlg <- "validation" on every matching trial in triplet_list – retroactively turning triplets that happened to be judged by many participants into genuine validation trials, for legacy data collected before this package's sampleAlg == "validation" convention existed.

Usage

assign_validation_from_frequency(
  triplet_list,
  freq_triplets,
  max_per_participant = Inf,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

triplet_list

Named list of per-participant triplet data frames, the same object passed to find_frequent_triplets.

freq_triplets

A data frame with a triplet column identifying which triplets to promote – normally the (optionally filtered) return value of find_frequent_triplets. All thresholding on "how often is often enough" happens there (via its own n/ min_participants arguments, or by filtering its output yourself) – this function does no frequency filtering of its own, it just applies whichever candidate set it's given. Row order matters when max_per_participant is finite – see Details.

max_per_participant

Integer (or Inf, the default). Caps how many distinct candidate triplets any one participant can have promoted to "validation" – see Details for why this is a per-triplet cap, not a per-row one, and how it interacts with freq_triplets' row order.

verbose

Logical. Print a short summary (how many triplets/trials were promoted, and any participants with none at all)? Default TRUE.

Value

triplet_list with sampleAlg updated for promoted trials; a list of the same length, names, and row order as the input. No other column is touched – in particular, sampleSet is left exactly as it was. Call set_validation_behavior on the result afterward (mode = "holdout" is almost always what you want – see Details) to actually exclude the newly-promoted trials from training and model selection.

Details

Why no frequency threshold lives here. find_frequent_triplets's own documentation already makes the case for deciding "how often is often enough" by inspecting its n_participants column, rather than picking a number blind. A reasonable starting point for data with enough participants to support it: require at least 5 participants per candidate triplet, the same ballpark this package's own bundled real validation sets reach (see icon_triplets) – but this depends heavily on total sample size and should be checked against the actual distribution of n_participants in your data (table(find_frequent_triplets(triplet_list, n = Inf)$n_participants) is a quick way to see it) rather than assumed.

Why max_per_participant exists and defaults to Inf. Every trial promoted to "validation" is (assuming you then call set_validation_behavior with mode = "holdout", as recommended above) one fewer trial available to train and test that participant's own embedding. A participant who happens to have judged many of the candidate triplets could lose a large, disproportionate share of their data this way with no cap in place. There's no universal right number – it depends on how many trials each participant completed in total – so the default is Inf (no cap) rather than a guessed value, with the recommendation to set it deliberately, e.g. to roughly 5-10\

Why the cap counts distinct triplets, not rows. A participant who happened to judge the same candidate triplet twice (triplets are usually sampled independently at random in exactly the legacy data this function targets, so repeats do happen) has both of those trials promoted together or not at all – the cap is never allowed to split a repeated triplet's trials apart, since make.vmat's own documentation notes repeated validation trials are useful for assessing a participant's self-consistency, and keeping only one half of such a pair would quietly throw that away.

Why row order in freq_triplets controls which triplets get dropped under the cap. When a participant's matches exceed max_per_participant, the triplets kept are whichever appear earliest in freq_triplets. find_frequent_triplets already returns its rows sorted by decreasing frequency, so by default this means: when a participant must lose some candidate triplets to the cap, the ones kept are those shared with the most other participants – which is also what you want for the resulting validation set's own majority votes to be well-supported. Passing a freq_triplets you reordered yourself changes this priority accordingly.

Trials already marked sampleAlg == "check" are never promoted, regardless of whether their triplet appears in freq_triplets.

See also

find_frequent_triplets for building freq_triplets; set_validation_behavior for the usual next step.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
freq <- find_frequent_triplets(legacy_triplets, n = Inf, min_participants = 5)
legacy_triplets <- assign_validation_from_frequency(
  legacy_triplets, freq, max_per_participant = 30
)
legacy_triplets <- set_validation_behavior(legacy_triplets, mode = "holdout")
} # }
